grade.basis: Independent whole-work assessment from all nine PDF spreads of the complete imposed Merton Music score (printed music pages 3–15, both halves inspected). I, Allegro espressivo: long chromatic, dynamically shaped phrases, upper-register shifts and exposed sustained intonation, largely in straightforward note values. II, Scherzo/Allegro assai with Trio: repeated high notes, accented and detached strokes, leaps, rests and clean ensemble re-entry. III, Larghetto: sustained singing line with slurred semiquaver decoration and chromatic passagework over moving inner voices. IV, Finale/Vivace: recurring upper-register quaver figures, slur/detache contrasts, quick shifts, chromatic sequences and repeated articulated high notes, with longer stretches of activity than the earlier movements. Violin 1 consistently has the highest and most mobile writing; the other three parts require independent phrasing, offbeat accuracy, balanced chords and close chromatic intonation. The material calls for secure advanced technique, comparable in overall demand to the level-5 La Folia and Haydn Rider/Emperor anchors, above the level-4 Bach Double baseline, but without the sustained virtuoso passagework or pervasive multiple-stopping that would support a higher band. Coordination is real but does not receive an automatic ensemble uplift. Medium confidence reflects a score-based assessment with approximately one level of remaining tempo/performance uncertainty; no prior numerical opinions were consulted.

scoreEvidence.coverage: All nine PDF spreads; printed music pages 3–15 contain all four movements through the final double bar. Imposed spread order was followed by printed page numbers.
scoreEvidence.method: Visual inspection of actual notation throughout all movements, with both halves checked.

entries.limits: Musical grading only. Identity, repertoire-floor and recording acceptance are outside this judgment and were not re-researched.
